name: Natural Language Processing: An Applied Research Practicum From Classical Text Processing to Multimodal and Agentic Systems

raw_payload.title: Natural Language Processing: An Applied Research Practicum From Classical Text Processing to Multimodal and Agentic Systems
raw_payload.summary:
This preprint presents a systematic, research-oriented guide to modern natural language processing, covering the full NLP pipeline from tokenisation, text normalisation, vector representations, and classical machine learning to transformer architectures, large language models, retrieval-augmented generation, preference-based alignment, and multimodal systems.
  The material comprises eighteen practical works combining theoretical foundations, reproducible implementation examples, detailed experimental procedures, evaluation metrics, and research-oriented assignments. Each work includes three structured core tasks and optional advanced investigations. Common requirements for reporting, data provenance, experimental evaluation, and reproducibility are established across the guide.
  Particular attention is devoted to low-resource and morphologically rich languages, including Tajik, Tatar, and Bashkir. The guide addresses subword tokenisation, cross-lingual transfer, machine translation, language model adaptation, and the evaluation of NLP systems under limited data and computational resources.
  Advanced topics include prompt engineering, reasoning strategies, multi-agent collaboration, model compression, efficient inference, AI safety, and LLMOps. A capstone project integrates methods from different chapters into the development and evaluation of domain-specific NLP systems.
  The guide is intended for senior undergraduate students, graduate students, researchers, and developers interested in implementing and critically evaluating NLP methods.
